key_insight: This study evaluates a pathology foundation model combined with multiple instance learning to grade Barrett’s esophagus dysplasia across institutions without stain normalization. It uses 969 whole-slide images from four institutions; the provided abstract does not report performance results.
problem_solved: Pathologists often disagree on dysplasia grades, especially low-grade dysplasia, complicating clinical decisions. The study addresses automated grading across institutions where tissue-staining appearance can vary.
method: Conduct a retrospective, multi-institutional diagnostic accuracy study using 969 H&E-stained whole-slide images.
Train patch-level classifiers on expert annotations to identify diagnostically relevant tissue regions.
Combine a pathology foundation model with multiple instance learning for dysplasia grading without stain normalization.
impact: The study examines whether foundation-model representations can support multi-institutional pathology workflows without stain normalization. For AI/ML practitioners, it highlights cross-site evaluation and learning from diagnostically relevant patches, although the supplied excerpt does not establish accuracy or clinical readiness.

paper_title: Multi-institutional grading of Barrett's esophagus dysplasia without stain normalization using a pathology foundation model and multiple instance learning
paper_authors: Amirali Khosravi, Jaidip M. Jagtap, D. Chamil Codipilly, Catherine E. Hagen, Jason T. Lewis
